payload.title: 8-Week Beginner Fat-Loss Full-Body Program (Dumbbell and Bodyweight, Knee-Friendly)
payload.summary: An 8-week, 3-day-per-week full-body program (Tuesday/Thursday/Saturday, about 35-40 minutes per session) for a beginner whose goal is fat loss, using only adjustable dumbbells (about 2-20 kg per hand) and bodyweight at home. All knee-dominant work is kept shallow-to-moderate because of pain with deep knee bending. Week 1 is a ramp-in at 2 sets per exercise, weeks 2-7 build volume and effort using double progression, and week 8 is a lighter deload. An optional easier week is available if you feel unusually fatigued around weeks 4-5.

constraints.description: Pain with deep knee bending; avoid deep squats/lunges and deep knee flexion under load. Keep knee range of motion shallow-to-moderate. No other injuries.

requirements_recap.notes: Home training. Adjustable dumbbells approx. 2-20 kg per hand. Schedule: Tuesday/Thursday/Saturday.

weekly_schedule.label: Day 1 (Tuesday) - Full Body A
weekly_schedule.focus: Full body, push and hinge emphasis; shallow-range knee-dominant work only (knee-safe)

weekly_schedule.label: Day 2 (Thursday) - Full Body B
weekly_schedule.focus: Full body, pull and single-leg/hip emphasis; loaded carry for conditioning (knee-safe)

weekly_schedule.label: Day 3 (Saturday) - Full Body C
weekly_schedule.focus: Full body, balanced push/pull with higher-density circuit-style finish for energy expenditure

safety_notes: Knee precaution: you have pain with deep knee bending. Keep knee bend shallow-to-moderate (pain-free, box-limited), and do not do deep squats, deep lunges, or loaded deep knee flexion. No loaded squats or lunges are programmed. Stop any movement that reproduces knee pain.
Bodyweight Squat: limit depth to a pain-free shallow-to-moderate range (box or well above parallel); stop if knee pain recurs.
Dumbbell Bent-Over Row and Romanian Deadlift: neutral spine, hinge at the hips; reduce load if your lower back fatigues.

Pull exercises: Dumbbell Bent-Over Row (db_row) is the only available dumbbell/bodyweight pull exercise suitable for a beginner. Bench-based rows (single-arm row, chest-supported row) are excluded because you have no bench; Renegade Row is advanced and loads the wrists. db_row is therefore used in all three sessions, varied by rep range and tempo.
Week 1 is a ramp-in (2 sets per exercise, about 3 reps in reserve). Week 8 is a deload (about 4 reps in reserve, lighter load or easier pace). Never train to true failure as a beginner.
Optional easier week: if you feel unusually fatigued or sore around weeks 4-5, drop to 2 sets per exercise at about 3 reps in reserve for one week, then continue.
If knee pain persists, see a clinician. The research sources are general-audience and secondary, and this program is not clinical or medical advice.
Nutrition is the main driver of fat loss and is outside the scope of this program. Optional knee-friendly activity on off days: walking, cycling, or swimming.

progression.strategy: Double progression within each exercise's rep range (per research.json finding for beginner fat-loss training: moderate rep ranges, 1-3 RIR, dumbbell loads capped around 20 kg). Week 1 starts one set lighter on 3-set exercises, weeks 2-7 run the prescribed sets while RIR tightens from 3 to 1-2, and week 8 is a lighter consolidation/deload. Once rep-range tops are reached, add load in small steps, or, when dumbbells cap out, add tempo, pauses, or shorter rest. Knee flexion stays shallow-to-moderate throughout. If you feel unusually fatigued or sore around weeks 4-5, take an easier week (drop to 2 sets per exercise at about 3 RIR) before continuing.
progression.optional_easier_week: Weeks 4-5, if unusually fatigued: 2 sets per exercise at about 3 RIR for one week

sources: Exercise catalogue: exercise-db MCP server (search_exercises, get_equipment_alternatives, list_equipment_categories)
source_caveats: Research sources are secondary fitness-media or summary articles, not primary studies or clinical advice; confirm details against primary sources (e.g. the ACSM position stand) if citing exactly.
Nutrition is outside the scope of this program.
